question: Ranjeet Singh belonged to which Misal of the Sikh community?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sukarchakia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ranjeet Singh, also known as Maharaja Ranjeet Singh, was the founder of the Sikh Empire in Punjab.
 
• He belonged to the Sukarchakia Misal, one of the prominent Misals (confederacies) of the Sikh community during the 18th century.
 
• The Sukarchakia Misal was named after its founder, Nawab Sukha Singh.
 
• Ranjeet Singh successfully unified various Sikh Misals and established a powerful empire, with Lahore as its capital.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Misal**

 
 
• A Misal was a sovereign state or confederacy in the Sikh tradition, each led by a different chief or leader known as a Misaldar.
 
• There were 12 prominent Misals in the 18th-century Sikh confederacy, including Sukarchakia, Ahluwalia, Kanhaiya, and Bhangi.
 
• These Misals were primarily military and political organizations that played a crucial role in defending Sikh territories against external invasions.
 
 
 
• **Maharaja Ranjeet Singh**
 
 
• Born on 13 November 1780, Ranjeet Singh became the leader of the Sukarchakia Misal after his father's death.
 
• He is credited with establishing a unified Sikh Empire in the early 19th century, encompassing parts of present-day India and Pakistan.
 
• His reign marked the consolidation of the Sikh territories and the establishment of a strong and efficient administrative system.
 
• Ranjeet Singh's leadership and military prowess earned him the title of "Sher-e-Punjab" (Lion of Punjab).
 
 
 
• **Lahore**
 
 
• Located in present-day Pakistan, Lahore served as the capital of the Sikh Empire under Maharaja Ranjeet Singh.
 
• The city became a center of cultural, economic, and political activities during his reign.
 
• Ranjeet Singh's administration brought about significant developments in infrastructure, including the construction of roads, canals, and forts.
 
 
 
• **Sikh Empire**
 
 
• The Sikh Empire was a major power in the Indian subcontinent during the early 19th century.
 
• It was established by Maharaja Ranjeet Singh, who unified various Sikh Misals and expanded the empire's territory through conquests and alliances.
 
• The empire's administration was known for its secular policies, promoting religious tolerance and inclusivity.
 
• The Sikh Empire eventually fell to the British East India Company in the mid-19th century, following the Anglo-Sikh wars.
